title: Mirabel and the Current
premise: Ada Thackeray, a salvage diver drowning in debt, takes a contract to survey a wreck the navy officially denies exists. When she recovers a chest bearing the seal of a nation that no longer appears on any map, she and her loyal deckhand Mirabel become targets of both the navy and the exiles who claim the chest holds proof of a massacre the world agreed to forget. Pursued downriver, they must run the current upstream to the wreck's true origin — a flooded archive at the river's forbidden source — before monsoon season seals it forever. Ada must choose between selling the truth to clear her debt or exposing it at the cost of everything, and in the end she gives the evidence to the exiles, sinking her own salvage boat and her old life with it.
about_author: Felix Whitlock is the pen name of a former merchant marine who spent six years working river salvage contracts across Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about water, debt, and the things governments leave at the bottom of rivers.

chapters.title: The Wreck They Don't Name
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Deep in debt to a harbor boss, Ada accepts a navy-adjacent salvage survey on a wreck no one will discuss. Diving alone, she finds a sealed chest stamped with a dead nation's crest — and cuts it loose against orders. The emotional beat is hungry ambition curdling into dread as she surfaces to find a naval patrol boat already waiting for her.

chapters.title: What the River Owes
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The patrol 'inspection' turns into an interrogation; Ada and Mirabel flee downstream with the chest, pursued by both the navy and a scarred exile named Suri who claims the chest proves her people were drowned deliberately decades ago. Torn between loyalty to Ada and the truth Suri tells, Mirabel opens the chest — and finds documents that make the lie undeniable.

chapters.title: Against the Current
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With the monsoon days away, they abandon the delta and fight upstream toward the flooded archive at the river's source, where the documents can be authenticated. A naval gunboat traps them in a gorge; Ada bargains with a smuggler lord who wants the chest for himself, buying passage at a price that means betraying either Suri or Mirabel. The beat is loyalty stretched to breaking.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the source, Ada dives the flooded archive herself and retrieves the full record of the massacre — then faces the navy commander offering to erase her debt if she surrenders it. She refuses, hands the evidence to Suri, and scuttles her own boat to block the pursuing gunboat in the narrows. The beat is costly justice: truth delivered, survival redefined, and Ada walking away owning nothing but her name.
